summary.value: Link component, renders a native `a` element.

a11y.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, human-reviewed 2026-08-11 (batch 2: agent first-pass, ratified)

value.rule: Put trigger words early in link text; vague phrases must not be the entire link text
value.quote: Use the important words (trigger words) early in the link text. “Go to”, “Click here”, “Link to” or “Read more” should never be the entire link text.

value.rule: All links on the same page must have unique link text
value.quote: All links on the same page must have unique link text.

value.rule: A verb should appear early in the link text
value.quote: A verb should appear early in the link text.

value.rule: Use text, not an icon, to explain where a link leads, since text is clear for both sighted users and screen reader users
value.quote: Instead, we always recommend using text to explain where the link leads. This makes the function clear both for users and for screen readers.

value.rule: Link text must make sense on its own when read aloud by a screen reader, regardless of surrounding context
value.quote: When writing link text, imagine it being read aloud by a screen reader. The text must make sense on its own, whether it appears in a sentence, menu or list.

relations.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, human-reviewed 2026-08-11 (batch 2: agent first-pass, ratified)

value.note: Use a button instead of a link when the user should perform an action on the same page, e.g. "Save" or "Submit"
value.quote: Avoid link when the user should perform an action on the same page, for example “Save” or “Submit”, use a button instead

value.note: Use a button instead of a link when the action changes the state of the solution, such as opening a dialog, starting a process or saving data
value.quote: the action changes the state of the solution, such as opening a dialog, starting a process or saving data, use a button instead

value.note: Use a button, not a link, when the action itself performs the operation (e.g. "Log in" that submits a login form) rather than navigating to a URL
value.quote: Use a button when “Log in” actually logs the user in, for example by submitting a login form.

composition.method: drafted from the docs page, quote-verified, human-reviewed 2026-08-11 (batch 2: agent first-pass, ratified)

value.rule: A link is often used inline as part of a text
value.quote: A link is often used as part of a text.

value.rule: An icon in a link can be placed left or right of the text; left is recommended
value.quote: Links can have an icon placed either to the left or the right of the text. As a general rule, we recommend placing the icon on the left.

value.rule: Neutral-coloured links are useful when placed in an area that has its own background colour
value.quote: This can be useful when the link is placed in an area with its own background colour.

value.rule: Avoid overusing links on a page, as this makes it harder for users to find their way forward
value.quote: It is important not to overuse links, as this can make it harder for users to find their way forward.
